newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish R&D share in GDP at 0.38 percent in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Turkish R&D share in GDP at 0.38 percent in 1995.

text.p: The share of research and development (R&D) in Turkey's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) edged higher to 0.38 percent in 1995 from 0.36 percent in 1994, but remained far below the ratios in developed countries, the State Institute of Statistics said on Thursday.
It said total R&D spending stood at 29.5 trillion lira last year, up from 14 trillion in 1994. In dollar terms, the increase was far less -- $1.30 billion in 1995 versus $1.15 the previous year.
R&D spending per capita also slightly firmed to $21.1 in 1995 after $19.1 a year ago.

It said 69 percent of the 1995 R&D spending was made by state universities, 23.6 percent by the private sector and 7.4 percent by the public sector. 62.4 percent of the 1995 R&D spending was publicly financed and 32.9 percent privately.
